public_rationale: On the contextual reading that excludes OpenAI as a customer, Microsoft had a meaningful AI business: its latest pre-post quarterly disclosure reported more than 20 million paid Microsoft 365 Copilot seats. That is substantial commercial adoption, even without assigning a dollar value to it. This does not establish that the business was profitable or technologically independent of OpenAI.
limitations: The result depends on the customer-based reading of outside of OpenAI.
Paid seats are company-reported and do not disclose realized revenue, discounts, or profit.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Excluding OpenAI, Microsoft has essentially no meaningful AI business.

statement.excerpt: Outside of OpenAI, Microsoft may as well not have an AI business.

from_speaker: Microsoft may as well not have an AI business
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that Microsoft lacks a commercially meaningful AI business beyond OpenAI as a paying customer.
The surrounding discussion of OpenAI's Azure spending supports excluding that customer, rather than excluding every Microsoft product that uses OpenAI technology.
Use Microsoft's fiscal third quarter ending March 31, 2026, its latest reported quarter before the post.
Assess commercial scale through paid adoption. Do not convert seats into revenue using undisclosed prices or infer profitability.
The exact claim asserts business significance rather than a particular monetary measure, so metric_scope is null.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes that Microsoft's AI business beyond OpenAI consists only of negligible paid adoption or commercially insignificant activity.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporaneous evidence establishes substantial paid adoption of Microsoft's AI products beyond OpenAI's own infrastructure purchases.
